title: One-Time Pad
description: Find the 64th one-time pad key by scanning MD5 hashes for triplets confirmed by a matching quintuplet within the next 1000 hashes.
writeup:
## Approach

This is a hash-stream search problem. For each index we compute `MD5(salt + index)` and look for a *triplet* (three consecutive identical characters). A triplet is only confirmed as a key if one of the next 1000 hashes contains a *quintuplet* of that same character.

The critical implementation detail is **caching**: confirming a triplet at index `i` requires hashes `i+1` through `i+1000`, many of which will also be needed as candidates themselves. Without caching every hash is computed multiple times. A simple dict keyed on index keeps each hash computed exactly once.

Regex makes triplet detection clean: `r"(.)\1\1"` matches any character repeated three times, and `.group(1)` gives the character to watch for.

## Part 1

Scan indices from 0 upward, caching MD5 hashes. For each triplet found, check the next 1000 hashes for the matching quintuplet. Collect until the 64th confirmed key; its index is the answer.

## Part 2

*Key stretching*: instead of one MD5, each hash is re-hashed 2016 additional times (2017 total). The logic is identical — only the hash function changes. This is intentionally expensive, slowing brute-force attacks; in Python it takes a few seconds even with caching.
